title: Improve README: Expand Usage Section with Real Examples
body:
## Improve README: Expand Usage Section with Real Examples

### Summary

The current Usage section in the README is a placeholder. It shows the general CLI syntax (`hxc [command] [options]`) and lists two generic example commands (`command1`, `command2`) that don't reflect the actual tool at all. A first-time user reading it has no idea how to initialize a registry, create their first project, or do anything meaningful with the tool.

---

### Problem

The current Usage section reads:

```
### Available Commands
- `command1`: Example command
- `command2`: Another example command
```

This is boilerplate left over from the project scaffold. It does not reflect the real commands (`init`, `create`, `list`, `show`, `get`, `edit`, `delete`, `validate`, `registry`, `mcp`) and gives the user zero guidance on how to actually use HoxCore.

---

### Tasks

Rewrite the Usage section to cover the essential workflow a new user needs to get started. At minimum it should include:

**1. Available Commands**

Replace the placeholder list with the real command reference:

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `init` | Initialize a new registry |
| `create` | Create a new entity (project, program, mission, action) |
| `list` | List entities with optional filters |
| `show` | Show full details of a specific entity |
| `get` | Get a specific property from an entity |
| `edit` | Edit properties of an entity |
| `delete` | Delete an entity from the registry |
| `validate` | Validate registry integrity |
| `registry` | Manage registry location |
| `mcp` | Start the MCP server for LLM access |

**2. Quick Start: Initialize a Registry**

Show the user how to create their first registry:

```bash
# Initialize a registry in the current directory
hxc init

# Initialize in a specific directory
hxc init ~/my-registry

# Initialize without git
hxc init --no-git
```

**3. Quick Start: Create Entities**

Show the most common creation examples:

```bash
# Create a project
hxc create project "My First Project"

# Create a project with description, tags and due date
hxc create project "API Redesign" --description "Redesign the public API" --tags backend api --due-date 2025-06-01

# Create a program (container for projects)
hxc create program "Q2 Initiatives"

# Create a mission (execution-oriented, time-bound)
hxc create mission "Deploy v2.0"

# Create an action (ongoing, no end date)
hxc create action "Monitor system health"
```

**4. Quick Start: List and Inspect**

```bash
# List all projects
hxc list project

# List all entities
hxc list all

# Filter by status
hxc list project --status active

# Filter by tag
hxc list project --tag backend

# Show full details of a specific entity
hxc show <uid>

# Get a specific property
hxc get <uid> status
hxc get <uid> tags
```

**5. Quick Start: Edit and Delete**

```bash
# Change status
hxc edit <uid> --set-status completed

# Add a tag
hxc edit <uid> --add-tag backend

# Set due date
hxc edit <uid> --set-due-date 2025-06-01

# Delete an entity (will prompt for confirmation)
hxc delete <uid>

# Delete without confirmation prompt
hxc delete <uid> --force
```

**6. Getting Help**

```bash
# General help
hxc --help

# Command-specific help
hxc create --help
hxc list --help
```

---

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Placeholder `command1` / `command2` references are removed
- [ ] All real commands are listed with a one-line description
- [ ] README includes a working Quick Start showing: init → create → list → show
- [ ] All code examples use real command syntax that actually works
- [ ] Examples are tested manually before merging to confirm they produce the expected output
- [ ] A new version is published to PyPI so the updated README appears on the package page

---

### Notes

- Keep examples simple and focused on the happy path — edge cases and full option references belong in a future dedicated docs site or wiki, not the README.
- Use a real UID placeholder like `<uid>` consistently so users understand they need to substitute it with an actual value from their registry.
- Consider adding a one-paragraph intro before the examples that explains the mental model: registry → entities (program / project / mission / action) → files on disk. This context helps users understand what they are creating before they run any commands.

---

### Labels
`documentation` `good first issue`

title: Cross-Platform Compatibility Fixes (Windows & macOS)
body:
## Cross-Platform Compatibility Fixes (Windows & macOS)

### Summary

HoxCore was developed and tested on Linux. A compatibility audit identified several issues that affect Windows and, to a lesser extent, macOS users. This issue tracks all required fixes before the next release.

---

### Problems Found

#### 🔴 High — Missing `encoding='utf-8'` on all file I/O

**Affects:** Windows (and any system where the default locale is not UTF-8)

Python's `open()` uses the system locale encoding by default. On Windows this is typically `cp1252`, not UTF-8. Any registry YAML file containing non-ASCII characters (accented letters, special symbols in titles or descriptions) will either raise a `UnicodeDecodeError` or silently corrupt data on read/write.

Affected files:
- `src/hxc/commands/cmd_list.py`
- `src/hxc/commands/create.py`
- `src/hxc/commands/edit.py`
- `src/hxc/commands/show.py`
- `src/hxc/commands/get.py`
- `src/hxc/commands/delete.py`
- `src/hxc/commands/validate.py`
- `src/hxc/mcp/resources.py`
- `src/hxc/mcp/tools.py`
- `src/hxc/core/config.py`

**Fix:** Add `encoding='utf-8'` to every `open()` call. Also add `allow_unicode=True` to all `yaml.dump()` calls so non-ASCII characters are written as-is instead of being escaped as `\uXXXX` sequences. Add `ensure_ascii=False` to `json.dump()` calls for the same reason.

---

#### 🔴 High — No check for Git availability before running subprocess commands

**Affects:** Windows (Git is not pre-installed)

In `src/hxc/commands/init.py`, `hxc init` runs `subprocess.run(["git", "init", ...])` unconditionally. On Windows machines where Git is not installed or not on PATH, this raises an unhandled `FileNotFoundError` and crashes with no user-friendly message.

**Fix:** Use `shutil.which("git")` before any git subprocess call. If git is not found, print a descriptive warning with the install URL (`https://git-scm.com`) and skip git initialization gracefully. The registry itself should still be created successfully.

---

#### 🟡 Medium — Hardcoded `master` branch name

**Affects:** All platforms

In `src/hxc/commands/init.py`, the git push command hardcodes `master` as the branch name. Modern Git installations default to `main`. This causes the initial push to fail silently on systems configured with `main` as the default branch.

**Fix:** Detect the actual branch name dynamically using `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` after the initial commit and use that value in the push command.

---

#### 🟡 Medium — Git subprocess output mixed into hxc terminal output

**Affects:** All platforms

All `subprocess.run()` git calls in `init.py` print directly to stdout/stderr, mixing git's verbose output with hxc's own formatted messages. This makes the terminal output confusing and unprofessional.

**Fix:** Add `capture_output=True` and `text=True` to all git subprocess calls. Surface error output only on failure via the `CalledProcessError` exception, which should be caught and displayed with a clean warning message.

---

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All `open()` calls include `encoding='utf-8'`
- [ ] All `yaml.dump()` calls include `allow_unicode=True`
- [ ] All `json.dump()` calls include `ensure_ascii=False`
- [ ] `hxc init` prints a friendly message when git is not found, and completes successfully without it
- [ ] `hxc init` detects the default branch name dynamically instead of hardcoding `master`
- [ ] Git output is not printed to the terminal during `hxc init`
- [ ] All existing tests pass on Windows and macOS
- [ ] Manual test: create a registry entry with non-ASCII characters on Windows and verify it reads back correctly

---

### Verification

After applying fixes, run the following from the project root to confirm no `open()` calls are missing encoding:

```bash
grep -rn "open(" src/hxc/ | grep -v "encoding=" | grep -v "__pycache__"
```

Expected result: no output.

---

### Labels
`bug` `cross-platform` `windows` `good first issue`
